takeaway: Over 40 per cent blood loss with extreme tachycardia, a collapsing pressure and unconsciousness is Class IV shock.

question.text: A 45-year-old man arrives after a road accident: pulse 160 beats/min, BP 75/50 mmHg, unresponsive. Which degree of haemorrhagic shock?
question.say: A forty-five-year-old man arrives after a road traffic accident. His pulse is one hundred and sixty beats per minute, his blood pressure is seventy-five over fifty, and he is unresponsive. Which degree of haemorrhagic shock is this?

lines.text: The heart drums frantically: pulse 160, an extreme tachycardia.
lines.say: The heart is drumming frantically. The pulse is one hundred and sixty beats per minute, an extreme tachycardia.

lines.text: The blood pressure gauge is collapsing: 75/50.
lines.say: The blood pressure gauge is collapsing: seventy-five over fifty.

lines.text: And he is unresponsive, unconscious on the trolley.
lines.say: He is unresponsive, lying unconscious on the trolley while the team rushes around him.

lines.text: The drip bag is almost empty: over 40 per cent of the blood is lost.
lines.say: (sigh) The drip bag is almost empty. More than forty per cent of the circulating blood is gone.
That is class four shock, the most severe degree.

lines.text: Remember: extreme tachycardia, collapsing pressure, unconscious means Class IV.
lines.say: Remember: extreme tachycardia, a collapsing pressure and unconsciousness mean class four shock.
